unit.why: A narrative: a young Hasid's anti-Hasidic, learned father-in-law mocks his trips to the rebbe and his dietary stringency, then travels with him to argue, and the rebbe answers both objections with homilies.

stories.start_quote: להרב הצדיק הנ״ל היה מקורב אברך
stories.end_quote: אסור לו סירכא אבל לא לכל העולם
stories.summary_en: A learned non-Hasidic father-in-law mocks his son-in-law for travelling to the rebbe and for refusing meat with a sircha; he goes along to dispute with the rebbe, who answers with an exegesis of Jethro's coming to Moses (one needs the tzaddik against the evil inclination) and an analogy from the High Priest's stricter marriage laws.
